strap: A daily dispatch from the world you are entering

lead.title: A state has decided the private house is a workplace, and from 2027 every nanny, cook and household manager in Washington will work under a written contract
lead.standfirst: Washington's Domestic Workers Bill of Rights takes effect on 1 July 2027 and reaches anyone who pays for domestic work in a private residence for more than four hours in a month.
lead.body:
House Bill 2355 was signed into law on 9 March 2026 and takes effect on 1 July 2027. It makes no distinction between a staffing agency placing candidates and a family hiring directly: if you pay someone to perform domestic work in a private residence for four or more hours in any calendar month, you are a hiring entity with legal obligations. The definition of domestic worker is deliberately broad and names nannies, caregivers, housekeepers, cooks, gardeners and household managers.

The central requirement is the written work agreement. It must set out pay, schedule, duties and benefits, and it must be provided in the language the worker speaks most comfortably. The Washington Department of Labor and Industries has been given the intervening period to draft model agreements and guidance, which is why the law was written with a delayed start rather than an immediate one. Alongside the contract come state minimum wage, overtime for hours above forty in a week, and verifiable payroll records.

The provisions on ending an engagement are the ones most likely to change behaviour in large houses. Employers must give two weeks of written notice to most domestic workers and four weeks to live-in workers, or pay severance equal to the missed notice period, subject to narrow exceptions. The law also reaches into the fabric of the house itself. Monitoring is prohibited in bathrooms, private living quarters and dressing areas, private communications are protected, and employers may not take or hold passports or personal documents.

Enforcement is where the drafting bites. Any adverse action taken within ninety days of a worker asserting a right, whether that is dismissal, reduced hours or a pay cut, is presumed retaliatory, and the burden then sits with the household. Anti-discrimination protections apply regardless of employer size, which means a family employing one person is covered on the same terms as an agency employing two hundred. Penalties payable to the state can reach from USD 20,000 to USD 40,000 for repeat violations.

Washington is not the first jurisdiction to legislate in this area, and a federal Domestic Workers Bill of Rights Act sits in both chambers of Congress, but the state has produced the most complete template so far for what compliance actually looks like inside a private residence. Households with property in more than one state will find the highest standard travelling with them, because a single set of contracts and payroll practices is easier to run than several.
lead.why: The written work agreement, the payroll record and the notice letter are documents somebody in the house has to draft, hold and produce on request. In most households that person is the estate manager or the house manager, and this law turns that administrative habit into a legal defence.

articles.title: Manhattan's luxury market signed thirteen contracts in a week, the thinnest holiday week the borough has recorded in three years
articles.body:
Olshan Realty has tracked every signed contract on a Manhattan home asking USD 4 million or more, week by week, for decades, and the count is one of the few genuinely high frequency readings anyone has on the top of an American housing market. Between 31 August and 6 September 2026, buyers signed thirteen of them.

The asking price total across those thirteen contracts was USD 66 million, the lowest weekly figure since September 2023. The previous week had produced twenty four deals. The decade average for the equivalent holiday week is sixteen, so the market came in below its own seasonal floor rather than merely below a strong month.

The composition matters more than the headline. Only one of the thirteen was a new development unit, at a moment when the new development pipeline in Manhattan is already shrinking, and not one contract was signed on a home asking USD 10 million or above. The most expensive property to find a buyer was a loft style duplex at 61 North Moore Street in Tribeca, asking USD 6.5 million, which had come to the market in July.

A single week around Labour Day proves very little on its own, and the same tracker recorded a run of strong weeks earlier in the summer. What it does show is the rhythm the top of the market still keeps. Principals are out of the city in late August, the people who advise them are too, and nothing above USD 10 million gets signed until the households come back.
articles.why: That rhythm governs the private staff calendar as much as the brokerage one. The weeks when nothing is signed are the weeks when the New York house is closed, the staff are travelling with the family or covering a summer property, and the estate manager schedules the works that cannot be done while anyone is in residence.

articles.title: The autumn sales are built on a handful of very large pictures, and every one of them carries a legal history attached
articles.body: The consignments announced for the autumn season are, in the phrase used by advisers canvassed this month, masterpiece heavy. Sotheby's has secured the Blaquier Collection, valued at around USD 450 million, a group of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist works including Van Gogh, Degas, Pissarro and Renoir, released for sale after a legal dispute over its export from Argentina. The full lot list has not been confirmed, but a work from Cezanne's Harlequin series is thought capable of exceeding USD 120 million, and a Van Gogh chestnut tree canvas is discussed in the range of USD 150 million to USD 200 million. Christie's has announced two headline Modernist lots for its 20th and 21st Century evening sale during London's Frieze Week. One is a Piet Mondrian, Composition III of 1922, never before offered at auction, estimated at GBP 20 million to GBP 30 million. The other is Wassily Kandinsky's Das bunte Leben of 1907, newly restituted after a decade long legal battle and expected to fetch more than USD 30 million. The pattern is consistent. Three of the season's defining consignments reach the saleroom because a dispute over ownership, restitution or export was resolved first. Provenance is not a footnote in the catalogue this autumn, it is the reason the material is available at all. Advisers remain cautious about what this proves. The momentum coming out of the May sales in New York and June's Lewis Collection sale in London has been concentrated at the very top, on trophy lots, and the open question is whether it reaches the day sales at all. Tariffs and wider macroeconomic volatility were both named as things that could still dampen confidence before December. Beyond the salerooms, the fair calendar is crowded: Art Basel Paris is the season's priority for most advisers, with the inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi and Art Week Tokyo both falling in November.
articles.why: A household that holds pictures holds paperwork. The provenance file, the export licence, the loan agreement and the insurance schedule are documents the private office keeps and the house manager is often asked to find, and this season is a reminder of how much value can turn on whether they are in order.

articles.title: The largest yacht ever built is due before the year ends, and the 2026 delivery list is unusually heavy at the top
articles.body:
REV Ocean, built by Vard and measuring 194.9 metres with a volume of 19,235 gross tonnes, is officially expected for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2026 after a cumulative construction period of more than eight years. Exterior and interior design came from Espen Oino and H2 Yacht Design. She has been at Damen Shiprepair in Vlissingen for a final outfitting period of fifteen to eighteen months, and on delivery she will be available for charter through Burgess.

She is the largest of a top-heavy year. Also scheduled for 2026 are Project Tanzanite, a 120 metre Amels that becomes the largest Dutch built motor yacht in history at 6,083 gross tonnes; Boardwalk, a 117 metre Lurssen commissioned in 2022; and Project Cosmos, a 114.2 metre Lurssen fitted with two 500 kilowatt methanol fuel cells, among the first yachts in the world to carry fuel cell technology. Admiral's 100 metre Hull 597 becomes the Italian yard's flagship.

The number that should interest anyone working in service is on Project Vela, a 130 metre sailing yacht under construction at Brodotrogir in Croatia. She is expected to accommodate twelve guests and carry a total of fifty crew. Four crew to each guest is not unusual at this size, and it is a useful corrective to the assumption that a larger boat simply means a larger cabin.

Each of these hulls represents an interior department to be recruited, trained and housed, on top of a deck and engineering complement, and the yards are delivering them within months of one another. The interior crew market has been tight at senior level for two years. A year like this one does not loosen it.
articles.why: Yachts of this size are staffed at ratios no house can match, and they compete for the same people. A chief stewardess or a private chef who moves to a 120 metre new build is not returning to a land based household that season.

articles.title: Admiralty Arch takes overnight guests for the first time in its history, with 114 rooms at the ceremonial end of The Mall
articles.body:
Waldorf Astoria London at Admiralty Arch opens this autumn, with reservations already live for stays from 1 March 2027. The Grade I listed monument stands at the end of The Mall opposite Buckingham Palace, spans 200,000 square feet, and was commissioned by King Edward VII in memory of Queen Victoria to a design by Sir Aston Webb, the architect of the Buckingham Palace facade. It has never before accommodated overnight guests. The restoration has been carried out by Reuben Brothers in partnership with Hilton.

There are 114 rooms, suites and residences, with residential and signature suites occupying more than half of the accommodation space. The names follow the building's naval history: the Nelson Suite, the St James's Residence and the Victory Residence, the last named after HMS Victory.

The dining is the part of the project that will interest a private household's address book. Coreus, set within the former home of the First Sea Lord, is Clare Smyth's fine dining concept built around British coastal produce and sustainably sourced seafood, with an intimate whisky and seaweed bar attached. Cafe Boulud, on the rooftop, marks Daniel Boulud's return to London with an all-day format and a terrace looking across St James's Park towards Buckingham Palace. Between them the two chefs hold eight Michelin stars.

Event space includes a ballroom of 3,540 square feet accommodating up to 500 guests, reached by the building's original oval staircase and hung with a nine metre antique Murano chandelier restored in Rome. A spa with individual and couples' treatment rooms, sauna, steam room and hydrotherapy pool completes the plan.
articles.why: Households with London business need somewhere to place visiting family, and an address on The Mall during a state occasion is a booking that will be requested long before it is available. The residence-heavy room mix is the point: guests who travel with staff need suites, not rooms.

briefs.t: Asia Week opens the New York season
briefs.b: Six houses, Bonhams, Christie's, Doyle, Freeman's, Heritage and Sotheby's, hold their autumn Asian art sales in New York this week, with Bonhams running from 14 to 16 September and Christie's from 15 to 18 September. Christie's offers Hiroshige: Colors of the Four Seasons, from the Alan Medaugh Collection, with 180 prints in the opening sale alone. It is the first substantial test of appetite before the November marquee sales.

briefs.t: Arthur Jafa at the New Museum, from 25 September
briefs.b: The New Museum opens a survey of the American artist Arthur Jafa on 25 September in New York. He also co-headlines with Richard Prince in Helter Skelter at the Fondazione Prada in Venice, running through November. Advisers expect his work to appear across fairs and salerooms this season, which makes him a name worth knowing before a principal mentions it.

briefs.t: What an American estate manager is worth
briefs.b: The United States average for an estate manager stood at USD 188,217 a year as of 1 September 2026. Published guides place entry level roles at USD 85,000 to USD 120,000, mid-career at USD 120,000 to USD 165,000, and managers with ten years or more at USD 180,000 to USD 250,000 plus benefits. Total compensation for domestic and travelling staff typically runs from 15 to 40 per cent above base once accommodation, travel and bonuses are counted.
